sub_answers.sub_question: What degeneracies exist between eccentricity, mass ratio, spin, and distance in gravitational-wave parameter estimation?
sub_answers.text: Eccentricity is partially degenerate with mass ratio and spin because inclusion of higher-order modes and eccentric corrections changes signal morphology and affects recovery of these parameters [d79698s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What astrophysical formation channels predict high-eccentricity black hole mergers and how uncertain are their event-rate predictions?
sub_answers.text: Hierarchical triple systems in globular clusters and galactic nuclei are predicted to produce mergers with observably large eccentricity [d42403s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant sources of systematic error (waveform model inaccuracies, detector calibration, selection effects) affecting H0 from GW events like GW190521?
sub_answers.text: Inaccuracies and incomplete coverage of eccentric waveform models are a dominant systematic because different waveform families cover only portions of parameter space and produce differing sensitivities and parameter recovery [d101479s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How do limited sky localization and lack of electromagnetic counterparts constrain host identification and redshift determination for GW190521?
sub_answers.text: Limited sky localization degrades the ability to identify a unique host galaxy and thereby prevents secure redshift assignment for events without electromagnetic counterparts [d110908s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How would revising GW190521's inferred luminosity distance under an eccentric-merger model change its contribution to a gravitational-wave H0 posterior?
What statistical methods combine single-event distance measurements from gravitational waves into joint H0 estimates, and how sensitive are they to outlier events?
sub_answers.text:
Eccentric binaries can introduce large phase shifts that differ from quasicircular waveforms, which can make an event appear as an outlier in analyses that assume circular orbits [d51623s0p0].
Ignoring eccentricity in waveform models can lead to significant apparent deviations in parameter inference and model tests, indicating sensitivity of analyses to outlier signals with nonzero eccentricity [d86122s0p0].
Limited coverage of eccentric waveform families restricts the ability to model and correctly infer parameters for eccentric events, increasing vulnerability to outliers when combining events [d101479s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How can eccentric-merger interpretations affect the use of galaxy catalogs or redshift priors when associating GW190521 with host galaxies?
sub_answers.text:
Incomplete or inaccurate waveform modeling of eccentric mergers reduces the precision and accuracy of distance and orbital-parameter estimates that underpin host-galaxy association with catalogs [d101479s0p0].
Eccentricity-driven phase and timing differences can shift inferred source parameters relevant for matching to galaxy redshifts, complicating the use of galaxy catalogs or redshift priors for host identification [d51623s0p0].
Because eccentric signals can mimic unexplained deviations when analyzed with circular templates, it becomes necessary to consider eccentric interpretations when assigning host probabilities from catalog matches [d86122s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What practical changes in data analysis pipelines are required to incorporate eccentric waveform models into standard siren H0 inference?
sub_answers.text:
Pipelines must incorporate eccentric waveform models and expand waveform banks to cover eccentric parameter space to avoid bias from mis-modeled signals [d101479s0p0].
Analysis must account for eccentricity-induced phase shifts and mode excitations by using models or simulations that capture those effects to maintain accurate parameter and distance inference [d51623s0p0].
Validation against numerical-relativity and post-Newtonian comparisons for eccentric systems is required to ensure waveform fidelity and phase agreement near merger [d2843s0p0].
Pipelines should include explicit tests for eccentricity to prevent misinterpreting eccentric signals as deviations from baseline models or physics assumptions [d86122s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What were the reported primary observational properties (masses, spins, sky localization, luminosity distance) of GW190521?
sub_answers.text: GW190521 was a binary black hole merger for which an electromagnetic candidate counterpart ZTF19abanrhr was reported at redshift z = 0.438 [d61893s0p0]. GW luminosity-distance estimates for GW190521 were obtained using multiple waveform models (NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv4PHM, IMRPhenomPv3HM) and used to infer cosmological parameters [d61893s0p0]. H0 estimates derived from GW190521 using those waveform-dependent luminosity distances were reported as medians with large credible intervals (e.g., 50.4+28.1/-19.5, 62.2+29.5/-19.7, and 43.1+24.6/-11.4 km s^-1 Mpc^-1 for the three waveforms) [d61893s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What observational signatures distinguish an eccentric binary black hole merger from a circular one in gravitational-wave data?
sub_answers.text: Eccentric binaries exhibit oscillatory frequency evolution that makes gravitational-wave frequencies recur multiple times through coalescence, unlike quasi-circular inspirals [d110908s0p0]. Eccentric mergers can excite additional dynamical features such as f-mode oscillations and produce different matter-ejection signatures compared to quasi-circular mergers in neutron-star systems, yielding distinct waveform content and potential electromagnetic differences [d107535s0p0]. Eccentric signals can be substantially shorter in time than quasi-circular signals yet can produce equal or larger signal-to-noise ratios in advanced LIGO–type detectors for moderate eccentricities [d60694s0p0]. Eccentric binaries tend to circularize in the last few cycles before merger, which can make the late-merger and ringdown waveforms resemble circular-merger waveforms [d39658s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What is the physical definition of the Hubble constant (H0) and how is it estimated using gravitational-wave standard sirens?
sub_answers.text: The Hubble constant H0 quantifies the present-day expansion rate of the Universe and is reported in units of km s^-1 Mpc^-1 in the cited analysis [d61893s0p0]. Gravitational-wave standard-siren estimates of H0 are obtained by combining the GW-measured luminosity distance with an electromagnetic redshift from an identified counterpart or host galaxy to infer the cosmological expansion rate [d61893s0p0]. Marginalization over other cosmological parameters (e.g., matter density Omega_m or dark-energy equation-of-state w0) and combination with additional events can tighten constraints on H0 from standard-siren measurements [d61893s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are typical detection sensitivities and selection biases of LIGO/Virgo for high-mass, short-duration signals like GW190521?
sub_answers.text: Identification of eccentric mergers with LIGO/Virgo is challenging in part because of the limited availability of eccentric waveform models covering the full parameter space, which affects sensitivity and parameter estimation for high-mass short-duration signals [d101479s0p0]. Sensitivity to eccentric signals depends on eccentricity, total mass, and mass ratio, and these dependencies must be quantified to understand detection prospects and population constraints [d101479s0p0]. For advanced LIGO–type detector networks, eccentric mergers with moderate initial eccentricity can produce larger SNRs than quasi-circular mergers even when their signal durations are much shorter, which biases detectability toward some eccentric systems [d60694s0p0]. The tendency of eccentric binaries to circularize before merger means late-time signals can resemble circular mergers, complicating selection effects and waveform-modeling requirements for high-mass, short-duration events [d39658s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does nonzero orbital eccentricity modify the gravitational-wave waveform morphology compared to quasi-circular templates?
sub_answers.text: Eccentric binaries produce oscillatory frequency evolution with recurrent passages of the same GW frequencies during coalescence, unlike the monotonic chirp of quasi-circular templates [d110908s0p0]. Eccentricity induces amplitude, phase, and frequency modulations across spherical harmonic modes that are related by a common eccentric modulation time series [d94650s0p0]. Eccentric systems can excite f-mode oscillations at pericenter that transfer energy into stellar oscillations and advance the GW phase relative to circular inspirals [d51623s0p0]. Inclusion of subdominant modes is more important for eccentric systems and alters sky localization and signal-to-noise compared to using only the (2,2) mode [d110908s0p0][d79698s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the effects of eccentricity on measured source-frame versus detector-frame masses and inferred redshift?
How does eccentricity-induced waveform complexity affect Bayesian parameter estimation and distance uncertainty for compact binaries?
sub_answers.text: Orbital eccentricity can be degenerate with other low-frequency effects such as line-of-sight acceleration unless both effects are modeled in the waveform, impacting parameter recovery [d131516s0p0]. When both eccentricity and LOSA are included in templates, injected eccentric and LOSA parameters are recovered within the 90% credible interval in Bayesian analyses [d131516s0p0]. Including eccentricity and subdominant modes improves sky localization and can substantially reduce localization area and provide extra early warning time compared to neglecting eccentricity [d110908s0p0]. Inclusion of higher-order modes increases signal-to-noise and measurably affects the recovery of moderately and highly eccentric mergers, which influences distance and parameter estimation [d79698s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What waveform models and approximations exist for eccentric binary black holes and how do their systematic errors compare?
sub_answers.text: Eccentric waveform resources include numerical-relativity catalogs from SXS and RIT and semi-analytical models such as TEOBResumS-Dali, TEOBResumS, and SEOBNRE [d101479s0p0][d79698s0p0]. A modular model (gwNRHME) maps a quadrupolar quasi-circular waveform into a multi-modal eccentric waveform using a single eccentric modulation time series [d94650s0p0]. Available waveform suites currently cover only parts of the binary parameter space, limiting eccentric identification and searches [d101479s0p0]. Comparisons to NR simulations show the gwNRHME model achieves mismatches around 10^{-3}, comparable to NR numerical errors, indicating low systematic error for that method in tested cases [d94650s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which specific parameter correlations appear in GW parameter-estimation posteriors that couple orbital eccentricity with component mass ratio, individual and effective spins, and luminosity distance, what physical waveform features produce those covariances, and which observables or additional analyses most effectively break or reduce each degeneracy?
sub_answers.text: Orbital eccentricity can be degenerate with a line-of-sight acceleration term, producing covariances in phase evolution that can mimic eccentric-phase corrections in parameter-posteriors [d131516s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which astrophysical channels (e.g., dynamical interactions in globular/young/open clusters, nuclear star clusters and AGN disks, binary-single/binary-binary encounters, and Lidov–Kozai-induced mergers in triples) are predicted to produce black-hole binaries with measurable residual eccentricity at LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA frequencies, what typical eccentricity distributions do models give at 10–100 Hz, and how large and model-dependent are the corresponding merger-rate predictions and their major uncertainties?
sub_answers.text: Dynamical-capture and dynamical-encounter channels are predicted to produce highly eccentric black-hole mergers that are morphologically distinct from quasi-circular mergers and can yield measurable residual eccentricity in the detector band [d61816s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For a GW standard-siren inference of H0 based on a signal like GW190521, which systematic error terms contribute most to the distance-redshift uncertainty budget (e.g., imperfect waveform models including eccentricity/precession/multiple peaks, detector amplitude and phase calibration, selection and population priors, and possible host misidentification), what are their estimated magnitudes for a heavy, short signal like GW190521, and which of these currently dominate the systematic error budget?
sub_answers.text: Imperfect waveform models that omit eccentricity, higher modes, or dynamical-capture phenomenology are a major systematic because missing physics can produce biased parameter inference and false deviations from GR for eccentric signals [d86122s0p0][d101479s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Quantitatively, how do a large GW sky-localization area and absence of an electromagnetic counterpart limit confident host-galaxy identification and redshift assignment for GW190521-like events (e.g., typical sky area, localization-volume, number of plausible galaxies within photometric/spectroscopic catalogs at the inferred distance), what biases arise from relying on galaxy catalogs or a statistical galaxy-weighting approach, and which follow-up or analysis strategies (deep imaging, wide-field spectroscopic surveys, Bayesian host weighting) most reduce redshift/host ambiguity?
sub_answers.text: Including eccentricity and subdominant modes in waveform models can substantially reduce sky-localization areas and thereby reduce host ambiguity, with reported sky-area reductions of order a few to tens of percent up to large factors depending on eccentricity and detector configuration [d110908s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: If GW190521 is reanalyzed with an eccentric-merger waveform, how would the resulting shift in its luminosity-distance posterior (changes in median, credible interval, and multimodality) alter that event's likelihood weight in a combined gravitational-wave H0 posterior and the event's posterior odds for pulling the joint H0 mean away from the population average?
sub_answers.text: A shift in GW190521's luminosity-distance posterior will change the event's contribution to a joint H0 posterior because the per-event GW luminosity distance estimates were directly used to infer H0 from GW190521 when combined with an EM redshift [d61893s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which concrete statistical frameworks (hierarchical Bayesian combination, inverse-variance weighting, Bayesian model averaging, robust mixtures or heavy-tailed likelihoods) are used to combine per-event GW distance posteriors into a joint H0 estimate, and how can one quantify each method's sensitivity to a single outlying event (e.g., influence functions, leave-one-out posteriors, Bayes factors, jackknife or downweighting experiments)?
sub_answers.text: Bayesian parameter estimation and Bayesian model-comparison tools such as Bayes factors are used in related GW inference contexts and in deciding between hypotheses about signal properties [d114831s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Precisely how would interpreting GW190521 as an eccentric merger change the mapping between its GW distance posterior and external redshift information used for host association — for example by modifying the three-dimensional localization volume, the redshift likelihood used with galaxy catalogs (GLADE, DES, SDSS), the completeness correction, and the posterior probabilities assigned to specific catalog galaxies?
sub_answers.text: Using an EM counterpart redshift to map a GW distance posterior into an H0 measurement requires combining the GW luminosity distance posterior with the counterpart redshift, as done for ZTF19abanrhr at z=0.438 in the GW190521 H0 analyses [d61893s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What concrete modifications are needed in a standard-siren H0 analysis pipeline to support eccentric waveforms: changes to waveform libraries and approximants, updated parameter-estimation samplers and priors, computation of selection functions for eccentric templates, additional injection campaigns to calibrate detection efficiency, and any practical impacts on computational cost and convergence diagnostics?
sub_answers.text: A standard-siren pipeline must include eccentric waveform models in its waveform libraries because dedicated eccentric inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform prescriptions have been developed for non-spinning eccentric binaries [d39658s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the reported measured properties and their uncertainties for GW190521 from LIGO/Virgo analyses: detector-frame and source-frame component masses, total and remnant mass, mass ratio, individual and remnant spins (magnitudes and tilt/posteriors), sky localization area (credible regions), luminosity distance and redshift posteriors, network signal-to-noise ratio and Bayesian odds for competing waveform models; indicate which values depend strongly on waveform model choices (e.g., NRSur, IMRPhenom, SEOBNR).

Which observable features in gravitational-wave data and parameter-estimation outputs indicate a binary black hole merger had significant orbital eccentricity at detection rather than being quasi-circular: differences in phasing evolution (frequency evolution residuals), presence/strength of higher-order harmonics and periastron burst structure, mismatch with circular-template banks, recovered eccentricity posteriors (e.g., e at 10 Hz or at reference frequency), measurable eccentricity-induced modulation of amplitude/phase, and how these signatures compete with effects from spin precession or noise artifacts?
sub_answers.text:
Significant orbital eccentricity produces oscillatory or non-monotonic GW frequency evolution that deviates from quasi-circular phasing models and can appear as frequency-evolution residuals in parameter estimation [d110908s0p0].
Eccentric mergers generate periastron bursts and stronger power in higher-order harmonics, so detectable increases in subdominant modes or burst-like features in the waveform indicate eccentricity [d110908s0p0][d79698s0p0].
A poor match or systematic mismatch between signals and circular-template banks, and recovered posteriors favoring nonzero eccentricity values (e.g., e measured at a reference frequency like 10 Hz) indicate eccentricity [d101479s0p0][d60694s0p0].
Eccentricity-induced amplitude and phase modulations can mimic or compete with signatures of spin precession or detector noise transients, complicating attribution of residuals to eccentricity versus precession or artifacts [d110908s0p0][d86122s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the physical definition of the Hubble constant H0 (its role as the present-day expansion rate of the Universe with units km s^-1 Mpc^-1 and relation v = H0 d for recessional velocity at low z) and give a step-by-step description of how H0 is estimated using gravitational-wave "standard sirens": how luminosity distance is inferred from the GW amplitude and its posterior, how redshift is obtained (direct EM counterpart redshift or statistical comparison with galaxy catalogs / large-scale structure), handling of peculiar velocities and cosmic redshift–mass degeneracy, incorporation of selection effects and priors, and the Bayesian framework used to combine multiple events into a joint H0 posterior.

What are the typical LIGO/Virgo detection sensitivities and selection biases specific to high-total-mass, short-duration signals like GW190521: how search sensitivity (horizon distance and sensitive volume) depends on total mass and mass ratio, the effect of short signal duration and low number of GW cycles on matched-filter SNR and parameter recovery, frequency-band overlap with detector noise (e.g., most power at lower frequencies), typical false alarm rate thresholds and how pipelines treat short signals, detection bias toward face-on, unequal-spin or near-equal-mass systems, and quantitative examples or ranges (e.g., how sensitive distance/scalar reach changes between 60–300 Msun systems and corresponding detection completeness and parameter estimation biases).
sub_answers.text:
Search sensitivity and SNR depend strongly on total mass, mass ratio and waveform content, with interpolated SNRs varying across these parameters and enabling rapid population SNR calculations [d60259s0p0].
For advanced LIGO–type detectors eccentric mergers with moderate eccentricity (e0 ≤ 0.4 at 10 Hz) have equal or larger SNRs than quasi-circular systems even when their signal duration is much shorter, which affects horizon distance and sensitive volume estimates [d60694s0p0].
Including higher-order waveform modes increases SNR by a measurable amount (between ~3.5% and 35% for ℓ≤4 in studied cases), which is important for recovering parameters of short, high-mass or eccentric signals [d79698s0p0].
Short-duration, high-total-mass signals concentrate power at lower frequencies and have fewer GW cycles in band, reducing matched-filter phase information and degrading parameter recovery and localization compared to longer signals [d60694s0p0][d79698s0p0].
Detector networks and pipelines therefore exhibit selection biases favoring configurations that maximize SNR for short signals, and sensitive-distance behavior varies with total mass and eccentricity as shown by modeled SNR ranges across detector generations (e.g., differences between advanced LIGO, Cosmic Explorer and Einstein Telescope sensitivities) [d60694s0p0][d101479s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways do finite orbital eccentricities alter the time-frequency structure, harmonics, and phase evolution of gravitational-wave signals relative to the standard quasi-circular inspiral–merger–ringdown templates?
sub_answers.text: Eccentricity introduces multiple orbital harmonics and additional amplitude content in the Fourier-domain response compared to quasi-circular signals, with amplitude corrections computed to 1PN and harmonics included to high PN order in ready-to-use templates [d50914s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does nonzero eccentricity bias the conversion between detector-frame masses and source-frame masses via redshift estimates, and what specific shifts in inferred cosmological redshift or source-frame mass distributions have been reported?

To what extent does additional amplitude/phase modulation from eccentric orbits degrade Bayesian inference—e.g., posterior widths, multimodality, and correlations—and how does this propagate into uncertainties on luminosity distance for compact-binary signals?
sub_answers.text: Neglecting eccentricity can produce apparent deviations in parameterized GR tests and mimic beyond-GR effects, with modest eccentricities (∼0.05–0.1 at low frequency) producing significant false deviations in standard tests [d86122s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which families of eccentric waveform models (post-Newtonian eccentric templates, effective-one-body with eccentricity, numerical-relativity calibrated hybrids, kludge or quasi-Keplerian waveforms) are available for eccentric BBH systems, and what are the quantified systematic mismatches or parameter biases between these models and with full NR results?
sub_answers.text: Post-Newtonian-based analytic Fourier-domain eccentric templates that include amplitude corrections to 1PN and eccentric-phase terms up to high PN order are available for moderately eccentric inspirals [d50914s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which specific parameter degeneracies appear in gravitational-wave inference between orbital eccentricity, component mass ratio, individual spins (magnitude and tilt), and luminosity distance — how do these degeneracies show up in likelihood/posterior correlations, which waveform features (phase evolution, higher harmonics, periastron bursts) are most affected, and can you quantify typical degeneracy strengths from published PE corner plots or Fisher-matrix studies?
sub_answers.text:
Line-of-sight acceleration effects are degenerate with orbital eccentricity in the gravitational-wave phase if only one effect is modeled, producing correlated biases in parameter posteriors unless both are included in the template [d131516s0p0].
Including higher-order modes up to l=4 changes the recovery of moderately and highly eccentric mergers and therefore couples eccentricity inference with mass-ratio and spin recovery through modified mode amplitudes and phasing [d79698s0p0].
Neglecting eccentricity at the percent-to-tenth level (e.g., e~0.05–0.1 at low frequency) can produce significant apparent deviations in parameterized tests and thus indicates strong posterior bias from unmodeled eccentricity in realistic PE studies [d86122s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which astrophysical channels (e.g., few-body dynamical captures in globular clusters and nuclear star clusters, binary-single interactions, Kozai–Lidov-driven mergers in hierarchical triples, black-hole migration and capture in AGN disks, or isolated stellar binary evolution with supernova kicks) are predicted to produce black-hole mergers with measurable residual eccentricity in the LIGO band, and what are the published event-rate ranges and main model assumptions/uncertainties (stellar densities, retention fractions, gas torque efficiency) that drive those rate uncertainties?
sub_answers.text:
Dynamically formed compact-object binaries are predicted to retain measurable residual eccentricity in the detector band for some formation channels and can excite tidal and oscillation effects that affect the waveform [d51623s0p0].
Studies emphasize that eccentric mergers are expected to comprise a significant fraction of detected events in some future scenarios, motivating targeted sensitivity and waveform development across mass, mass-ratio, and eccentricity [d110908s0p0].
The limited availability and parameter coverage of current eccentric waveform models restricts robust population-rate inference and contributes to major uncertainties in event-rate predictions and channel attribution [d101479s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: For measurement of the Hubble constant from single GW events like GW190521, which systematic error sources dominate the uncertainty budget — specifically how large are contributions from incomplete waveform models (neglecting precession, eccentricity, higher modes), detector amplitude/phase calibration errors, selection and Malmquist biases, weak lensing and peculiar velocities, and prior/population assumptions — and what published studies quantify the magnitude of each contribution and proposed mitigation strategies?
sub_answers.text:
Incomplete waveform models that neglect eccentricity, higher modes, or relevant physics can produce large systematic biases in inferred parameters and even false apparent deviations from general relativity in standard tests [d86122s0p0].
Degeneracies between line-of-sight acceleration and eccentricity can bias parameter recovery unless both effects are included in templates, and including both effects allows recovery within nominal credible intervals in injection studies [d131516s0p0].
The limited coverage of eccentric waveform families and missing subdominant modes reduce signal recovery and SNR by amounts that depend on mode content, with inclusion of modes up to l=4 increasing SNR by ~3.5%–35% for some systems and thereby affecting systematic error budgets tied to waveform incompleteness [d79698s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Given GW190521's broad sky localization and absence of an electromagnetic counterpart, how does that concretely limit identification of host galaxy and redshift: what is the typical sky-area and comoving-volume searched, how complete are galaxy catalogs at the relevant distance/redshift, how do probabilistic host-assignment methods (ranking by luminosity or stellar mass, cross-correlation) and photometric vs spectroscopic redshift errors propagate into redshift uncertainty, and what is the resulting impact on the inferred distance–redshift/H0 measurement?

If GW190521's luminosity distance posterior were recomputed using an eccentric-binary waveform model (e.g., fitting for eccentricity and periapsis parameters), how would the resulting distance distribution alter that event's likelihood contribution in a combined gravitational-wave measurement of H0?
sub_answers.text: Recomputing GW190521's distance posterior with an eccentric-binary waveform can shift the recovered distance because eccentricity modifies the GW phase evolution used to infer source parameters [d131516s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which hierarchical Bayesian estimators or meta-analysis techniques (e.g., inverse-variance weighting, full hierarchical Bayes with selection effects, Bayesian model averaging) are used to combine single-event GW distance posteriors into a joint H0 posterior, and how do these methods perform when one input posterior is discordant (quantify robustness using influence functions, Bayesian leave-one-out, or outlier-contamination simulations)?
sub_answers.text: Signals with unmodeled eccentricity can produce significant biases in parameter inference that could masquerade as other effects, which implies that a discordant input posterior from an eccentric model can materially affect combined inference robustness [d86122s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: When GW190521 is modeled as an eccentric merger, how would changes in its distance and sky-localization posteriors modify cross-matching with galaxy catalogs and the construction of redshift priors (for example, changes in galaxy weighting, completeness corrections, or the probability of host assignment within specific catalog volumes)?
sub_answers.text: Modeling eccentricity and external acceleration together resolves degeneracies and allows recovery of true parameters within the 90% credible interval in injection studies, which implies that properly modeled eccentric posteriors will be less outlying in hierarchical combinations [d131516s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What code and workflow modifications (specific steps such as replacing waveform families in parameter-estimation samplers, updating selection-effect calculations, reweighting posterior samples, and validating pipeline biases) are necessary to incorporate eccentric waveform models into standard-siren H0 inference pipelines used by LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA collaborations?
sub_answers.text: Including higher-order waveform modes and eccentric modulation can change the signal-to-noise and waveform morphology, which alters sky-localization and thus the weighting of candidate host galaxies in catalog cross-matching [d79698s0p0][d94650s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the reported quantitative observational properties of GW190521 from LIGO/Virgo analyses, including estimated source-frame and detector-frame component masses with uncertainties, total and remnant mass, component and remnant spins (magnitudes and tilt/alignments if reported), sky localization (credible region area and coordinates), estimated luminosity distance with credible interval and redshift estimates, plus any quoted measurement systematics or alternative parameter-estimation results (e.g., multimodal posteriors).
sub_answers.text: An electromagnetic candidate counterpart to GW190521 was reported as ZTF19abanrhr at redshift z = 0.438 [d61893s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which measurable gravitational-wave features are used to identify orbital eccentricity in binary black hole mergers — for example, changes to the inspiral phase evolution, excess power in higher harmonics or periastron bursts, modulation of time-frequency tracks, mismatch with circular templates, and parameter-estimation signatures — and what specific statistics or waveform models (eccentric templates, Bayesian model selection, residuals, Bayes factors) have been applied to distinguish eccentric from quasi-circular BBH events?
sub_answers.text: Eccentricity is diagnosed by measurable changes to the waveform phasing and morphology compared to circular inspirals, including oscillatory frequency evolution and recurring frequency passages through the detector band due to periastron passages [d101479s0p0][d110908s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give a concise physical definition of the Hubble constant H0 (H0 = (ȧ/a)0 — expansion rate today) including units and its relation to recessional velocity and distance, then describe in detail how gravitational-wave standard sirens estimate H0: how GW strain yields luminosity distance (including calibration and inclination degeneracies), the need for an independent redshift (EM counterpart, host galaxy identification, or statistical galaxy catalog association), the likelihood or Bayesian framework used, and major sources of uncertainty such as peculiar velocities, selection effects, and distance-redshift degeneracy.
sub_answers.text: Gravitational-wave standard-siren H0 estimates combine a luminosity distance measured from the GW strain with an independent redshift measurement from an electromagnetic counterpart or host-galaxy association [d61893s0p0][d31726s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Summarize LIGO/Virgo detection sensitivity and selection effects specifically for very high-mass, short-duration signals like GW190521: expected horizon and sensitive distance as a function of total mass and mass ratio, typical SNR and optimal SNR thresholds, time-frequency morphology (few cycles / merger-dominated), limitations of matched-filter pipelines vs unmodeled burst searches, template bank coverage and mismatch for high-mass or precessing/eccentric systems, biases in parameter recovery and detection efficiency (e.g., sky- and orientation-dependent selection, redshift-dependent incompleteness), and how these factors affect measured rates and population inferences for heavy BBHs.
sub_answers.text: Very high-mass BBH signals are short in duration and are merger-dominated, producing few inspiral cycles in band and concentrating power near merger, which affects matched-filter sensitivity and time-frequency morphology [d101479s0p0][d110908s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which specific amplitude, phase and harmonic features (e.g., power at multiple orbital harmonics, periastron bursts, secular phase shifts and periapsis precession) distinguish eccentric inspiral–merger–ringdown waveforms from quasi‑circular templates, and how do these features alter time‑frequency morphology and matched‑filter SNR at different eccentricities and mass ratios?
sub_answers.text: Eccentric waveforms contain power at multiple orbital harmonics and concentrated energy bursts near periastron passages, producing a sequence of bursts rather than a continuous quasi-circular signal [d22474s0p0][d50914s0p0].  Eccentricity modulates amplitudes, phases, and instantaneous frequencies across spherical-harmonic modes by a single time-series modulation, imprinting amplitude and phase oscillations on the waveform [d94650s0p0].  Eccentric binaries circularize in the last few cycles before merger so quasi-circular merger waveforms can be used when eccentricity is small at late times, but eccentricity up to e_ref≈0.08 affects inspiral cycles and waveform faithfulness [d39658s0p0].  For fixed masses and mass ratio, moderate initial eccentricities can increase or decrease matched-filter SNR relative to quasi-circular signals depending on detector sensitivity and eccentricity: advanced-LIGO SNRs for some eccentric mergers are larger than quasi-circular for e0≤0.4 at 10 Hz, while for third-generation detectors SNR differences depend on e0 and detector type [d60694s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways does nonzero orbital eccentricity bias the inference of detector‑frame masses and the conversion to source‑frame masses (and thus inferred redshift), including quantitative examples of mass and redshift shifts or degeneracies for moderately eccentric binaries at z≈0.1–1?
sub_answers.text: Eccentricity alters the gravitational-wave phase evolution and can advance the phase relative to circular models, which changes the mapping from detector-frame masses to intrinsic masses and redshift when circular templates are assumed [d51623s0p0][d50408s0p0].  Tidal and f-mode excitations in eccentric neutron-star binaries can produce cumulative phase shifts up to ~0.5 radians for initial eccentricities ~0.2 at 50 Hz, which would shift inferred masses or redshifts if unmodeled [d50408s0p0].  Modeling inaccuracies from neglecting eccentricity lead to systematic mismatches that can bias parameter recovery, and NR-calibrated eccentric models report faithfulness thresholds (e.g., >97% faithfulness for e_ref≲0.05 and M≥70 M⊙) that constrain when biases are small [d39658s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How does the added complexity from eccentricity (e.g., extra harmonics, short periastron bursts, faster phase evolution) change Bayesian parameter estimation behavior — posterior shapes, multimodality, Fisher‑matrix vs full sampling uncertainties, distance–inclination–eccentricity degeneracies — and what are typical impacts on luminosity‑distance uncertainty and parameter bias?
sub_answers.text: Extra harmonics and short periastron bursts increase waveform structure and can produce more complicated likelihood surfaces with potential multimodality and non-Gaussian posteriors in Bayesian inference when eccentricity is present [d22474s0p0][d94650s0p0].  Faster orbital decay from tidal excitation in eccentric systems advances phase and timing of pericenter passages, changing posterior correlations between phase, masses, and time parameters compared to circular binaries [d51623s0p0].  Detector networks and waveform models that include eccentricity can recover higher SNRs and more consistent parameters, whereas neglecting eccentricity produces systematic biases and enlarged uncertainties; ENIGMA studies show SNR and waveform-duration differences that affect parameter estimation for e0 up to ~0.4 [d60694s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What eccentric waveform families and approximations currently exist (post‑Newtonian eccentric inspirals, eccentric effective‑one‑body models, NR‑calibrated eccentric surrogates/hybrids, kludge models, time‑domain vs frequency‑domain approaches), what parameter ranges they cover, and what are their systematic errors/mismatches and resulting parameter biases reported in the literature?
sub_answers.text: Post-Newtonian eccentric inspiral templates exist with amplitude corrections to polarizations at 1PN and phase evolution up to 3PN including eccentricity effects to sixth order and periastron-advance prescriptions in the Fourier domain [d50914s0p0].  NR-calibrated eccentric inspiral-merger-ringdown models have been built and calibrated to NR simulations with e_ref≤0.08 and mass ratios q≤3, achieving >97% faithfulness in parts of parameter space and using circular merger interpolations due to late-time circularization [d39658s0p0].  Ready-to-use models like ENIGMA produce rapid waveforms across parameter space and report SNR behavior and applicability up to e0≈0.4 for Advanced-LIGO-type detectors, with reduced durations and differing SNRs compared to quasi-circular models [d60694s0p0].  Modular approaches convert quasi-circular multi-mode waveforms into eccentric ones using a universal eccentric modulation, yielding mismatches ~10^{-3} against NR in tested non-spinning cases [d94650s0p0].
